messages.subject: Use modules to update a data frame, and send back updated result to server.
parts:
Hi,

I am writing my first Shiny app, and my goal is to simply wrap some basic R functions to analyze and plot some data.
I would like to use modules to organize my code, but I have a problem right now, as I can not get updated data frame out of my module.

I read an ascii file (attached to the message) in my server. I would like then to perform clustering on this data in a separate module.
After te clustering is done, I would like to add a class column to my data frame, by pressing a button. Things seems to be ok within my clustering module, as my data summary shows the column with the right name.
However, it seems I can not return this data frame to my server, to then use in plots.

At the end of the day, I would like some modules to update my dataInput reactive data frame, and others to be updated accordingly (happends at the end of my server code below).

I spent quite some time on that without finding the solution, and being new to Shiny and reactive programming, I feel I reached my limits trying to find out alone.

My example below runs locally, I hope it illustrates my issue ok.

Thanks.

App UI code:
## app.R ##


options(autoWidth = TRUE)

header<- dashboardHeader(title = "Question?")

#Define content of sidebar
sidebar<- dashboardSidebar(
  sidebarMenu(
    selectInput(inputId="filetype",label="Specify file type",choices=c("CSV"=",","SKUA export"=" ")),
    checkboxInput("header", "Header", TRUE),
    fileInput(inputId="fileName",label="Select the file to work on:"),
    checkboxInput(inputId="standardize_data",label="Do you want to standardize data?",FALSE),
    menuItem("Input data Dashboard", tabName = "dash_board", icon = icon("dashboard")),
    menuItem("Clustering", tabName = "clustering", icon = icon("bug"))
  )
)

#Dasboard body definition. Gives content of each dashboard entry
body<-dashboardBody(
  tabItems(
    # First tab content
    tabItem(
      tabName = "dash_board",
      # Boxes need to be put in a row (or column)
      
      fluidRow(
        infoBoxOutput("info_var"),
        infoBoxOutput("info_lines")
      ),
      fluidRow(
        box(title="Debug",verbatimTextOutput("Debug"))
      ),
      fluidRow(box(title="Refresh Data"),  actionButton(inputId="Refresh", label="Refresh data")),
      fluidRow(
        box(title="Data frame", status = "primary", solidHeader = TRUE,
            collapsible = TRUE,
            tableOutput('contents'),width="100%")
      )
    ),
    tabItem(tabName="clustering",
            h2="Descriptive statistics on input data",
            kdash_clustering_UI("ClustUI")
    )
  )
)

#Run UI
ui <- dashboardPage(header,sidebar,body,skin="black")



Server Code:
options(shiny.maxRequestSize=100*1024^2)
options(autoWidth = TRUE)
source("./KDash_rainbow_palette.R")
source("./KDash_legend.R")

server <- function(input, output,session) {
 
  #load text file
  dataInput <- reactive({
    # input$file1 will be NULL initially. After the user selects
    # and uploads a file, it will be a data frame with 'name',
    # 'size', 'type', and 'datapath' columns. The 'datapath'
    # column will contain the local filenames where the data can
    # be found.
    inFile <- input$fileName
    
    if (is.null(inFile))
      return(NULL)
    
    dataIn<-read.table(inFile$datapath, header = input$header, sep=input$filetype)
    if(input$filetype==" "){
      dataIn<-dataIn[,1:ncol(dataIn)-1]
      if(input$standardize_data==TRUE){
        dataIn<-as.data.frame(scale(dataIn))
      }
    }else{
      if(input$standardize_data==TRUE){
        dataIn<-as.data.frame(scale(dataIn))
      }
    }
    
    
    dataIn
  })
 
  #render content of Info box for variable number and line number
  output$info_var <- renderInfoBox({
    infoBox(
      "Nb variables", ncol(dataInput()), icon = icon("list"),
      color = "navy"
    )
  })
  output$info_lines <- renderInfoBox({
    infoBox(
      "Nb lines", nrow(dataInput()), icon = icon("list"),
      color = "olive"
    )
  })
 
  #Render content of combo box containing variable names
 
 
  output$contents <- renderTable({
    dataInput()    
  })
 
  observeEvent(input$fileName,{
  #dataOutput<- eventReactive(dataInput(),{
  dataInput()<-callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput())
  })
 
  observeEvent(input$Refresh,{
  output$Debug<-renderPrint(head(dataInput()))
  })
}
 

Clustering Module:

kdash_clustering_UI<- function(id) {
  ns <- NS(id)
  fluidPage(
    fluidRow(
      box(title="Matrix plot of clustered data",
          plotOutput(ns("MatrixClust")),status = "primary", solidHeader = TRUE,
          collapsible = TRUE
      ),
      box(title="Clustering Controls",
          selectInput(ns("ClustMethod"),"Select clustering method",choices=c("Hierarchical-Ward","Hierarchical-Single",
                                                                             "Hierarchical-Complete","Hierarchical-Average(UPGMA)",
                                                                             "Hierarchical-McQuitty(WPGMA)","Hierarchical-Median(WPGMC)",
                                                                             "Hierarchical-Centroid(UPGMC)","KMeans"),multiple=F),
          sliderInput(ns("NbClust"),"Select Number of Classes",min=1,max=100,value=10),
          selectInput(ns("ClustVariables"),"Select variables to use for clustering","",multiple=T),
          actionButton(inputId=ns("SaveClusters"), label="Save Clusters"),
          status = "warning", solidHeader = TRUE,collapsible = TRUE)
    ),
    fluidRow(
      box(title="Summary statistics per class",width="100%",
          verbatimTextOutput(ns("SummaryClusters")),
          status = "primary", solidHeader = TRUE,collapsible = TRUE)
    )
  )
}

#Module code
kdash_clustering <- function(input, output, session, data) {
 
  #Get list of variables for select combo box. The selection defines which variable to keep for clustering
  observeEvent(data,{
    updateSelectInput(session=session, inputId="ClustVariables",choices = names(data))
  })
 
  #Create data structure with only variables to use for clustering
  clustering_data<-reactive({
    x<-names(data)
    y<-input$ClustVariables
    col_num <- which(x %in% y)
    clustering_data<-data[,col_num]
    clustering_data
  })
 
  #Segment flow based on hierarchical clustering linkage method
  data_hclust<-reactive({
    if (input$ClustMethod=="Hierarchical-Ward"){
      data_hclust <- hclust(dist(clustering_data()),method="ward.D")
    }else if(input$ClustMethod=="Hierarchical-Single"){
      data_hclust <- hclust(dist(clustering_data()),method="single")
    }else if(input$ClustMethod=="Hierarchical-Complete"){
      data_hclust <- hclust(dist(clustering_data()),method="complete")
    }else if(input$ClustMethod=="Hierarchical-Average(UPGMA)"){
      data_hclust <- hclust(dist(clustering_data()),method="average")
    }else if(input$ClustMethod=="Hierarchical-McQuitty(WPGMA)"){
      data_hclust <- hclust(dist(clustering_data()),method="mcquitty")
    }else if(input$ClustMethod=="Hierarchical-Median(WPGMC)"){
      data_hclust <- hclust(dist(clustering_data()),method="median")
    }else if(input$ClustMethod=="Hierarchical-Centroid(UPGMC)"){
      data_hclust <- hclust(dist(clustering_data()),method="centroid")
    }
    data_hclust
  })
 
 
  #Generate class vector. Does Classification if not hierarchical clustering. For Hierarchical clustering, handles dendogram cut in else statement.
  data_classes<-reactive({
    if(input$ClustMethod=="KMeans"){
      data_kmeans<-kmeans(clustering_data(), input$NbClust, nstart = 20)
      data_classes<-data_kmeans$cluster
      #output$SummaryClusters<-renderPrint(data_kmeans)
    }else{
      data_classes<-cutree(data_hclust(), k = input$NbClust)
      #output$SummaryClusters<-renderPrint(data_hclust())
    }
    data_classes
  })
 
  data_clustered<-eventReactive(input$SaveClusters,{
    data_clustered<-cbind(data,data_classes())
    setnames(data_clustered,"data_classes()",input$ClustMethod)
    data_clustered
  })
 
  output$SummaryClusters<-renderPrint(head(data_clustered())) 
 
  #Create or update matrix plot
  output$MatrixClust<-renderPlot({
    pairs(clustering_data(), col=data_classes(),cex=2,cex.axis=2, pch=16, main=paste("Matrix plot of ",list(input$ClustVariables) ,"using ",input$ClustMethod))
  })
return(data_clustered())
}

This topic has not been fleshed out enough in the documentation, sorry. You have the right idea, but some important fixes need to be made.

The `data` input parameter to your module server function, should not be a data frame; rather, it should be a reactive expression that yields a data frame. So instead of calling it like this from server.R:

callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput())

you should be calling it like this:

callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput)

The way to think of the original code is, "pass a snapshot of the current value of dataInput to kdash_clustering", while the corrected code is, "make all (current and future) values of dataInput available to kdash_clustering". And the latter is what you want.

Similarly, when returning data_clustered from inside kdash_clustering, you're saying "return(data_clustered())" when it should be "return(data_clustered)". Again, the former means "return a snapshot of the current value of data_clustered" when you really mean "make all (current and future) values of data_clustered available to whomever is calling me".

Then,

observeEvent(input$fileName,{
  #dataOutput<- eventReactive(dataInput(),{
  dataInput()<-callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput())
  })

should all be replaced by

dataClustered <- callModule(kdash_clustering, "ClustUI", dataInput)

and dataClustered() should be used in any reactive expressions or outputs or observers that want to access the post-clustered data.

You should also look into using req to deal with NULL values of input$fileName. https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/req.html

I hope that helps!

Hi Joe,

Thanks a lot for the explanations. It helped a lot. Now I am facing my next anticipated issue as I have several modules.

Once the data is clustered, I would like my other modules to be updated. I have some density plot and scatter plot modules, which can color per factor, so I would like the list of variables, and the data to be updated for them as well. So they should react to clustering process.

The solution I have found based on your help, is to pass 2 arguments to other modules.

 callModule(kdash_density,"DensPlots",dataInput,dataClustered)

 dataClustered<-callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput)

So my density plot module gets an updated list if dataClustered is not NULL. This works, but that requires to put some logic in the plot modules, and as many arguments as the nuber of modules susceptible to modify data (PCA module, standardization module, ...).

I tried in my server to do :
 observeEvent(input$Refresh,{
      dataInput<-dataClustered
      output$Debug<-renderPrint(head(dataInput()))
    })
That works, and displays my updated table, so I guess i can update dataInput.

However modules such as:
 
callModule(kdash_scatter,"Scatter",dataInput) keep the old list of variables from original dataInput, without added variable from clustering module.

I guess I do not use updateSelectInput correctly within the module:

#Scatter plot module

  observeEvent(data(),{
    updateSelectInput(session, "XAxis", choices = names(data()))

    updateSelectInput(session, "ZAxis", choices = names(data()))
    updateSelectInput(session, "ColorAxis", choices = names(data()))
  })
 }

I guess I am still missing a point on reactivity.

Basically what I did not manage to make work, is to replace dataInput by dataCluster, without the need to add an extra argument to my modules.

As I will implement several modules which will add to data or transform data, I would prefer to be able to overwrite dataInput, and make all modules react to that, rather than adding arguments for each possible transformation.

Thanks for your help.

This topic has not been fleshed out enough in the documentation, sorry. You have the right idea, but some important fixes need to be made.

The `data` input parameter to your module server function, should not be a data frame; rather, it should be a reactive expression that yields a data frame. So instead of calling it like this from server.R:

callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput())

you should be calling it like this:

callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput)

The way to think of the original code is, "pass a snapshot of the current value of dataInput to kdash_clustering", while the corrected code is, "make all (current and future) values of dataInput available to kdash_clustering". And the latter is what you want.

Similarly, when returning data_clustered from inside kdash_clustering, you're saying "return(data_clustered())" when it should be "return(data_clustered)". Again, the former means "return a snapshot of the current value of data_clustered" when you really mean "make all (current and future) values of data_clustered available to whomever is calling me".

Then,

  observeEvent(input$fileName,{
  #dataOutput<- eventReactive(dataInput(),{
  dataInput()<-callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput())
  })

should all be replaced by

dataClustered <- callModule(kdash_clustering, "ClustUI", dataInput)

and dataClustered() should be used in any reactive expressions or outputs or observers that want to access the post-clustered data.

You should also look into using req to deal with NULL values of input$fileName. https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/req.html

I hope that helps!

The first question I think you have to answer is whether the calculation modules *modify* the data frame, or *transform* it. The former implies that the original value is changed in-place, while the latter implies that a new copy is created by the module and downstream modules look at the new copy.

For example, say you have a module that does some smoothing on the data. If you take the former approach, you might have UI that consists of some smoothing parameters and a "Smooth" button; clicking the Smooth button modifies the original data. The advantage(?) is that you can perform this smooth multiple times, and in any order of operations relative to any other task being performed (like you can do it before or after you do some subsetting with a different module). The disadvantage is you can't undo the smoothing operation (at least not without a bunch more work).

If you take the latter approach, the UI might be just the smoothing parameters, no "Smooth" button to push (unless it is a very slow operation), and you can see what it looks like with different parameter values just by moving sliders around. The disadvantage is that you, the app author, need to decide when this smoothing should be performed relative to other modules like subsetting; the app user is not able to make their own decision about it (without doing a bunch more work).

This topic has not been fleshed out enough in the documentation, sorry. You have the right idea, but some important fixes need to be made.

The `data` input parameter to your module server function, should not be a data frame; rather, it should be a reactive expression that yields a data frame. So instead of calling it like this from server.R:

callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput())

you should be calling it like this:

callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput)

The way to think of the original code is, "pass a snapshot of the current value of dataInput to kdash_clustering", while the corrected code is, "make all (current and future) values of dataInput available to kdash_clustering". And the latter is what you want.

Similarly, when returning data_clustered from inside kdash_clustering, you're saying "return(data_clustered())" when it should be "return(data_clustered)". Again, the former means "return a snapshot of the current value of data_clustered" when you really mean "make all (current and future) values of data_clustered available to whomever is calling me".

Then,

  observeEvent(input$fileName,{
  #dataOutput<- eventReactive(dataInput(),{
  dataInput()<-callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput())
  })

should all be replaced by

dataClustered <- callModule(kdash_clustering, "ClustUI", dataInput)

and dataClustered() should be used in any reactive expressions or outputs or observers that want to access the post-clustered data.

You should also look into using req to deal with NULL values of input$fileName. https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/req.html

I hope that helps!

The first question I think you have to answer is whether the calculation modules *modify* the data frame, or *transform* it. The former implies that the original value is changed in-place, while the latter implies that a new copy is created by the module and downstream modules look at the new copy.

For example, say you have a module that does some smoothing on the data. If you take the former approach, you might have UI that consists of some smoothing parameters and a "Smooth" button; clicking the Smooth button modifies the original data. The advantage(?) is that you can perform this smooth multiple times, and in any order of operations relative to any other task being performed (like you can do it before or after you do some subsetting with a different module). The disadvantage is you can't undo the smoothing operation (at least not without a bunch more work).

If you take the latter approach, the UI might be just the smoothing parameters, no "Smooth" button to push (unless it is a very slow operation), and you can see what it looks like with different parameter values just by moving sliders around. The disadvantage is that you, the app author, need to decide when this smoothing should be performed relative to other modules like subsetting; the app user is not able to make their own decision about it (without doing a bunch more work).

#Module code
kdash_clustering <- function(input, output, session, data) {
 
  #Get list of variables for select combo box. The selection defines which variable to keep for clustering
  observeEvent(data,{
    updateSelectInput(session=session, inputId="ClustVariables",choices = names(data))
  })
 
  #Create data structure with only variables to use for clustering
  clustering_data<-reactive({
    x<-names(data)
    y<-input$ClustVariables
    col_num <- which(x %in% y)
    clustering_data<-data[,col_num]
    clustering_data
  })
 
  #Segment flow based on hierarchical clustering linkage method
  data_hclust<-reactive({
    if (input$ClustMethod=="Hierarchical-Ward"){
      data_hclust <- hclust(dist(clustering_data()),method="ward.D")
    }else if(input$ClustMethod=="Hierarchical-Single"){
      data_hclust <- hclust(dist(clustering_data()),method="single")
    }else if(input$ClustMethod=="Hierarchical-Complete"){
      data_hclust <- hclust(dist(clustering_data()),method="complete")
    }else if(input$ClustMethod=="Hierarchical-Average(UPGMA)"){
      data_hclust <- hclust(dist(clustering_data()),method="average")
    }else if(input$ClustMethod=="Hierarchical-McQuitty(WPGMA)"){
      data_hclust <- hclust(dist(clustering_data()),method="mcquitty")
    }else if(input$ClustMethod=="Hierarchical-Median(WPGMC)"){
      data_hclust <- hclust(dist(clustering_data()),method="median")
    }else if(input$ClustMethod=="Hierarchical-Centroid(UPGMC)"){
      data_hclust <- hclust(dist(clustering_data()),method="centroid")
    }
    data_hclust
  })
 
 
  #Generate class vector. Does Classification if not hierarchical clustering. For Hierarchical clustering, handles dendogram cut in else statement.
  data_classes<-reactive({
    if(input$ClustMethod=="KMeans"){
      data_kmeans<-kmeans(clustering_data(), input$NbClust, nstart = 20)
      data_classes<-data_kmeans$cluster
      #output$SummaryClusters<-renderPrint(data_kmeans)
    }else{
      data_classes<-cutree(data_hclust(), k = input$NbClust)
      #output$SummaryClusters<-renderPrint(data_hclust())
    }
    data_classes
  })
 
  data_clustered<-eventReactive(input$SaveClusters,{
    data_clustered<-cbind(data,data_classes())
    setnames(data_clustered,"data_classes()",input$ClustMethod)
    data_clustered
  })
 
  output$SummaryClusters<-renderPrint(head(data_clustered())) 
 
  #Create or update matrix plot
  output$MatrixClust<-renderPlot({
    pairs(clustering_data(), col=data_classes(),cex=2,cex.axis=2, pch=16, main=paste("Matrix plot of ",list(input$ClustVariables) ,"using ",input$ClustMethod))
  })
return(data_clustered())
}
